subject: Private VPC networking follow-up: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering and IP allowlists
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from the discovery call and next steps so we can get your Private VPC engagement moving: \n\nRecap of requirements you called out:
- HIPAA-covered PHI; strict egress controls required
- Prefer PrivateLink for control plane; some teams will need VPC peering for low-latency data transfer to an internal analytics VPC
- Need explicit IP allowlists and DNS resolution (private hosted zones)
- Customer-managed KMS, audit logging retained for 7 years

Immediate next steps I proposed:
1) Share our Private VPC networking checklist and a short network diagram (attached).
2) Confirm the VPC CIDRs you expect us to peer/connect to and whether you want cross-account peering or a Transit Gateway design.
3) Decide whether control-plane traffic should go over PrivateLink only. If yes, we’ll provide the PrivateLink endpoint configs.
4) Schedule a 30-minute networking sync with Sean (our infra network lead) to walk through firewall rules and NAT/egress patterns.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_requirements_v1.pdf (network checklist + diagram).

Questions for you to confirm:
- Preferred approach: PrivateLink-only for control plane, and VPC peering for data plane?
- VPC CIDR(s) for peering and the AWS account IDs (or a point of contact who can approve peering).
- Any specific IP ranges you need allowed (egress to third-party SaaS endpoints)?

If it helps, we can also provide a short statement-of-work outline and an estimated timeline once we confirm the network pattern.

Available times for the call: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT or Thu 1–4 PT. I’ll loop Sean in on replies.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

--

From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks for the detailed recap. Tom and I reviewed and answered inline below.

Short answers:
- We strongly prefer PrivateLink for control plane (security/compliance team is comfortable with endpoint models).
- For the data plane, a mix: some workloads will use VPC peering to our analytics VPC (10.20.0.0/16) for low latency; others can egress via NAT to the internet with strict allowlists.
- VPC CIDRs: ACME-Prod-VPC: 10.10.0.0/16 (AWS acct 123456789012), Analytics-VPC: 10.20.0.0/16 (same account).
- IP allowlists: we will need to allow outbound to a handful of Redwood IPs for model updates and logging; we also want to restrict egress so only approved third-party SaaS endpoints are reachable.
- KMS: We will provide a customer-managed key; we need docs for the required IAM role and key policy.

Attached: acme_vpc_inventory.csv (VPC IDs, subnets, route tables).

We are happy to do the 30 min networking call. Tom and I are available Wed 1/13 between 10–11 PT.

Thanks,
Alicia Park
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health
alicia.park@acmehealth.com

--
Attachment: acme_vpc_inventory.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up

Thanks Alicia — great, that helps a lot.

Technical notes and proposed approach:
- Control plane: PrivateLink endpoints into your account is our recommended default for HIPAA workloads because it avoids internet egress for control-plane API calls. We will provide the endpoint service name and the exact subnet requirements.
- Data plane: Use VPC peering for the Analytics-VPC (10.20.0.0/16) for low-latency inference responses; for other workloads, use NAT with allowlisted destinations.
- IPs: We’ll provide a short list of IPs/domains that need to be allowed outbound for model syncs/logging; we can also support an outbound proxy if you prefer a single egress IP.
- DNS: We recommend using private hosted zones and conditional forwarding for any internal service names.

Firewall sample (high-level):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: (redwood-control.*.amazonaws.com IPs) and customer-specific SaaS endpoints
- Allow inbound from peered VPC CIDR 10.20.0.0/16 to the service subnets
- No public ELB for control plane traffic; control calls should use the PrivateLink endpoint

I uploaded a short networking playbook with the exact security group/route table examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-networking (networking-playbook.md attached).

I’ll set the call for Wed 2027-01-13 at 10:15 PT with Sean and Tom unless you tell me otherwise.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachment: networking-playbook.md (markdown)

1) Can you confirm which subnets you prefer for PrivateLink (one per AZ) and whether those subnets have NAT gateways?
2) Please add a contact who can approve cross-account peering in case we need it (route table & security group changes require that approval).

Looking forward to Wed 1/13 10:15 PT — I'll send a calendar invite.
